svg.text: Spring Boot GraphQL API — Product Catalog (Spring for GraphQL, schema-first)
One reference diagram: Maven tree · UML class diagram · GraphQL schema (SDL) · execution flow · end-to-end trace. Single endpoint /graphql. Designed to be zoomed into.
dashed, open head = dependency (uses / returns / binds)
dotted indigo = schema binding (SDL type ↔ Java class/method)
Layer colour coding (consistent across all views)
@Argument binds a GraphQL argument · single endpoint POST /graphql
Single module. Note the SDL schema under resources/graphql — the source of truth.
2 · UML class diagram — resolvers, service, repositories, model
One @Controller holds all data-fetching methods. Nested fields (Product.category) are resolved by @SchemaMapping / batched by @BatchMapping.
«@BatchMapping» — loads all categories in one query (fixes N+1)
arguments bound by @Argument; return types match SDL fields
batch fetch avoids one query per product
«input DTO» bound from GraphQL input type
auto-detects schema + @Controller data fetchers on startup
SDL types auto-map to Java by name — wiring only for extras
adds extensions { code, path } to the error
GraphQL returns HTTP 200 with an "errors" array (not 4xx)
once per product → 1 + N database queries.
once for all → 1 + 1 queries (DataLoader batches keys).
Spring builds a DataLoader per @BatchMapping automatically.
resolves exceptions thrown by any @*Mapping data fetcher
2.5 · GraphQL schema — resources/graphql/schema.graphqls (the contract, single source of truth)
ID maps to Java Long/String; ! means non-null
object types → Product.java / Category.java (matched by name)
no versioning: clients ask for exactly the fields they need
Startup: Spring loads the SDL, then
wires each field to a matching handler
method. A field with no data fetcher
falls back to a property getter.
3 · Execution flow — one POST /graphql through the engine to the data fetchers
per field in the query, the engine invokes its data fetcher
collects all product ids in the tree, then loads every Category in ONE query → no N+1
engine assembles one JSON tree matching the query shape
• Validation uses the SDL, so bad
• One round trip fetches a whole graph;
4 · Request trace — a nested query · badges ①…⑧ map onto Region 3

g.text: Client POSTs one query document to /graphql (asking for only name, price, category.name).
The GraphQL HTTP handler hands the document to the graphql-java engine.
Parse — the query text becomes an abstract syntax tree (AST).
Validate against schema.graphqls — unknown fields/args are rejected before any DB call.
Execute root: product(id:1) → @QueryMapping product() → ProductService.findById → ProductRepository → DB.
Nested field category → @BatchMapping via DataLoader → CategoryRepository (one batched query, no N+1).
Engine assembles a JSON tree shaped exactly like the query (only the requested fields).
Returns HTTP 200 { "data": { "product": {...} } }; any errors go in a sibling "errors" array.

svg.text: // returns exactly these fields — nothing more, nothing less
Single self-contained SVG · viewBox 2600×2430 (rendered 5200×4860) · schema-first · layer-coloured across tree, classes, SDL and flow · standard UML notation.
